newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Chill wind blows Electrabel some good.
newsitem.headline: Chill wind blows Electrabel some good.

text.p: The chill winds of 1996 brought Belgian power utility Electrabel some cheer as electricity and gas consumption rose strongly, helping lift net profits by 5.5 percent despite price cuts.
Group net profit rose to 30.4 billion francs from 28.8 billion in calendar 1996 -- slightly ahead of analysts' forecasts of between 29.6 billion and 30.26 billion francs.
As expected the company followed its now traditional course of raising the net divided four percent to 352 francs per share.
Electrabel is controlled by holding company Tractebel through its Powerfin unit, both of which report their 1996 annual results on Tuesday.

The firm said electricity sales rose by 0.9 percent to 117.6 billion francs despite a price decrease in real terms amounting to 2.9 percent -- made up of a 0.9 percent price cut and 2.1 percent inflation.
It noted new price cuts had been implemented in January, representing savings to customers totalling 1.5 billion francs.
Sales of natural gas for public distribution climbed by 14.5 percent to 29.7 billion francs.

"The increase in volume sold is the result of gas' continuing market penetration and, especially, changing weather conditions," Electrabel said in a statement. "1996 was, on average, much colder than 1995."
However, also as expected, the 1996 bottom line was dented by a sharply higher tax charge -- up to 631 million francs from 281 million.
"The Belgian government needs the money. It wants to meet the Maastricht treaty (single currency) criteria," BBL analyst Guenter Klaffke told Reuters last week.

Electrabel invested a total of 46.4 billion francs -- mainly on building new steam and gas power stations, completing nuclear units and various cogeneration projects -- against 45.4 billion francs in 1995.
The firm's turnover in 1996 rose to 221.5 billion francs from 215.9 billion the previous year
